svg.text: Everyday English - Grammar
Hedging with might, seems
and tends to
MEANING
Use hedging to show appropriate uncertainty or
avoid making an overgeneralization.
IN CONTEXT
This approach might work better for smaller teams,
but it seems less practical at our current scale.
USAGE NOTE
Might + base verb signals possibility. Seems +
adjective or seems to + verb reports an impression.
Tends to + verb describes a usual pattern, not an
absolute rule. Do not hedge a verified fact so much
that it becomes unclear.
CONVERSATION
A: Will the new schedule solve the problem?
B: It might help. Demand tends to peak before lunch.
A: It seems sensible, but have we tested it?
B: Not yet. Let us try it for a week before drawing
conclusions.
YOUR TURN
Rewrite “This always works” as a careful statement
that explains when it may work and what still needs
testing.
